page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It provides 16 physical CPU cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU features a 35 MB L3 cache and supports Advanced Vector Extensions including AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), alongside AES hardware encryption and FMA bit manipulation. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, the server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and includes no bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks position the instance as a balanced environment for multi-threaded compute and network throughput. Across synthetic evaluations, PassMark CPU (27,240.11), Geekbench multi-core (10,181.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (127.99 GB/sec) consistently fall into average performance tiers. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 109.69 GB/sec, while uncached memory write bandwidth scales to 47.96 GB/sec. However, single-core processing metrics, such as single-threaded stress-ng and gzip compression, measure in lower percentiles. Network and database benchmarks demonstrate stable concurrency, achieving 26.78 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 20.38 GB/sec.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy applications due to its dense 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, avoiding unused RAM overhead in processing-focused setups. Because local disk storage is absent, storage dependencies rely entirely on attached cloud volumes. This compute profile suits workloads such as parallel software compilation, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, batch data processing, distributed application layers, and high-concurrency web serving.
